title: os
lede: Node-os-shaped operating-system information for portable CLI and microservice programs. The functions map onto real syscalls and /proc parsing rather than a fixed table, so os.cpus() returns live per-core tick counters on both Darwin and Linux. Two divergences are inherent to the host, not defects: os.cpus() speed is 0 on Apple Silicon (Apple dropped the fixed-clock model) and its Darwin times.irq is always 0, while os.EOL is always "\n" because this compiler is POSIX-only with no Windows target.

entries.name: os.platform()
entries.description: Returns the operating-system platform string. Reuses process.platform's existing runtime.GOOS-constant mechanism, so the two always agree.

entries.name: os.homedir()
entries.description: Returns the current user's home directory from getenv("HOME"). Throws a catchable Error if HOME is unset, matching real Node.

entries.name: os.tmpdir()
entries.description: Returns the default temporary-file directory from getenv("TMPDIR"), falling back to "/tmp". Never throws.

entries.name: os.hostname()
entries.description: Returns the host name of the operating system via POSIX gethostname().

entries.name: os.cpus()
entries.signature: cpus(): { model: string; speed: number; times: { user: number; nice: number; sys: number; idle: number; irq: number } }[]
entries.description: Returns real per-core {model, speed, times: {user, nice, sys, idle, irq}} objects — Linux via /proc/cpuinfo and /proc/stat parsing, Darwin via sysctlbyname and Mach host_processor_info — both verified (on Apple Silicon M4 Pro, model = "Apple M4 Pro" with live tick counters). On Linux, speed reflects the CPU's current/scaled frequency (from /proc/cpuinfo's cpu MHz), not a rated base/max clock, matching what libuv/real Node reports on Linux.
differences: Darwin `speed` is 0 on Apple Silicon — `sysctlbyname("hw.cpufrequency")` has no answer on M-series (Apple removed the fixed-clock model from M1 on); matches real Node's documented M-series behavior, not a defect.
Darwin `times.irq` is always 0 — Mach's per-core tick array has no `irq` bucket (only user/system/idle/nice).

entries.name: os.totalmem() / os.freemem()
entries.description: Return the total and free system memory in bytes. Verified on Linux and on Apple Silicon M4 Pro — totalmem() matches sysctl hw.memsize, and Darwin freemem() (Mach host_statistics) returns a live free-page figure.

returns.desc: Bytes of total or free memory.

entries.name: os.EOL
entries.description: The operating-system-specific end-of-line marker. Always "\n" — this compiler is POSIX-only (no Windows target), so there's no real "\r\n" case.
